children: Embraer and Mahindra Group plan to invest ₹6,000 crore in a C-390 Millennium aircraft final assembly line in Nagpur if selected to supply medium transport aircraft to the Indian Air Force (IAF).
The two groups signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Maharashtra government on Thursday evening selecting Nagpur as a location for the potential assembly line.

Chief Minister of Maharashtra Devendra Fadnavis’s office in a X post disclosed that this would result in an investment of ₹6,000 crore and create 1,000 jobs. The MOU was signed at the government’s Invest Maharashtra event.
The IAF is looking for a medium transport aircraft to replace the ageing fleet of AN-32 and IL-76 aircraft.

In August the defence ministry issued a request for proposal to Indian conglomerates such as Tatas, Mahindra, Adani and state run Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to submit their technical and financial offers.
While Embraer has teamed up with Mahindra group, Lockheed Martin has tied up with the Tatas to offer it’s C-130J aircraft.

“Mahindra is committed to building a globally competitive aerospace ecosystem in India and to creating meaningful manufacturing and technology capabilities that contribute to the country’s Atmanirbhar Bharat ambitions,” said Vinod Sahay, Member of the Group Executive Board, Mahindra Group.

Identifying Nagpur as the potential location for an assembly facility is an important step in building a robust, long-term aerospace ecosystem in the country,” said Bosco Da Costa Junior, President and Chief Executive Officer, Embraer Defense & Security.

The proposed Nagpur facility would be a state-of-the-art facility and a critical part of a broader industrialisation strategy in India bringing deep knowhow on aircraft assembly, system integration, manufacturing engineering, local supply chain development etc. into the country, the two companies said in a statement.

The partnership intends to progressively integrate Indian aerospace companies into the C-390 Millennium ecosystem, to deliver manufacturing, aftermarket services, training and lifecycle support, in line with the Government of India’s Make in India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat objectives,” they said.

Embraer and Mahindra entered into a Strategic Cooperation Agreement in October 2025 to jointly advance the C-390 Millennium for the IAF’s MTA programme, building on their earlier MoU signed in February 2024.

title: Embraer, Mahindra Group plan to invest ₹6,000 crore in Nagpur assembly line
